alignments.note: Waw to And.
Presentative וְהָיָה with its dummy subject and auxiliary (rule 21); the ASV writes no that for this first occurrence, so rule 45's third case leaves nothing to place.
כִּי takes the conditional if written for it (rule 55).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
Preposition to with.
Suffix to us (rule 18).
Waw rendered by the connective yea, which rule 14's open list reads off the ASV.

Corrected. The second presentative הָיָה keeps only its dummy subject and auxiliary. Its apodosis, וְהֵטַבְנוּ לָךְ, opens with a waw of its own (s018) after the fronted object phrase, so rule 45's second case governs and that waw, not the verb, carries the frame's complementizer.
The article is rendered by the determiner what standing where the phrase's the would stand (rule 41).
Substantival adjective to good.
The article on the resumptive pronoun takes the the of the same (rule 41).
The pronoun is rendered by the resumptive same.
The relative is rendered by the -soever that generalizes the head phrase; it is written for that morpheme and is not `added`.
Hiphil of יָטַב with its auxiliary; the good of its rendering is already written for הַטּוֹב, so the verb keeps shall do.
Explicit subject name.
Preposition rendered unto.
Suffix to us (rule 18).

Corrected. This is the apodosis waw of the second וְהָיָה, standing first in its clause after the fronted object phrase, so rule 45 gives it the frame's complementizer that; the unit is discontinuous from the rest of its clause under rule 25, the English writing the word at the frame's edge. The accepted alignment marked this waw `unrepresented` and gave the that to the verb, on the stated ground that no waw opened the apodosis, which the token table contradicts. The competing reading treats וְהֵטַבְנוּ as a coordinated clause rather than the apodosis, which would restore the accepted division.
Hiphil with its auxiliary and subject pronoun; the object of the doing is the resumptive same, so the verb keeps only will we do.
Lamed rendered unto.
Suffix to thee (rule 18).

review_notes: Corrected: the frame's that (t014) moves from the second הָיָה to the apodosis waw s018, which is no longer `unrepresented`. Rule 45 keys the disposition to the Hebrew — apodosis waw present, that waw takes the word — and v.35 in this same chapter applies that case, while v.11 applies the asyndetic case.
what good soever ... the same distributes over four morphemes: the two articles take what and the, the adjective takes good, the relative takes soever, and הוּא takes same.
Unlike v.29's do thee good, neither Hiphil here is headed on a complement, since good is written for the adjective הַטּוֹב rather than for the verb.
